column4: docs/spec/match_api.md states what lib/pcrec.h and every generated matcher actually promise, as shipped; it is the contract, not the design record.
References to docs/design/match_api_m4.md and docs/design/engine_m4.md are informational; they are never a second source of authority.
On any disagreement between match_api.md and match_api_m4.md/engine_m4.md, match_api.md is what pcrec promises.
CHECK: the §6.3 mirror (stamp macros mirrored into rx_info) is partial, not total.
The encoding residual entry <prefix>_next_pos is specified in §3.1.1, and the §3.1 find-all loop advances through it.

Measured: the §3.1 find-all loop compiled against real artifacts agrees with python3 re.finditer on 26 (pattern, subject) pairs x 2 engine arms (52 runs), with the lossy class checked as a strict subset in both directions (tests/encseam/).
CHECK: measured at the D56 refusal boundary between a{9795} and a{9796} (the refusal wording names an escape).
The encoding enumerator is spelled PCREC_ENC_BYTE (renamed from PCREC_ENC_ASCII).
The byte-vs-character caveat of the find-all loop is resolved by §3.1.1 (<prefix>_next_pos), not deleted.
The sort key of rx_info's groups array is strcmp on the group name, matching libpcre2's PCRE2_INFO_NAMETABLE order.
The groups array is sorted (by strcmp on name) and therefore bsearch-able.
Under --no-captures a named-groups build delivers group rows with slot -1; with captures on, rows carry a real slot.
On captures-on builds the primary groups' slot equals the group number permanently.
The latitude for a slot different from the group number applies only to future ref-bearing rows, not to primary groups.
rx_info.ngroups carries a PERMANENT-PREFIX promise: caps slots 1..ngroups are this pattern's own groups forever.
Mechanisms that insert groups (composition etc.) append after slots 1..ngroups and never interleave with them.
Every emitted macro whose value is a property of pcrec's contract rather than of one artifact has one canonical unprefixed PCREC_* spelling in the shared PCREC_RX_ABI_H block.
The give-up codes are spelled PCREC_ERR_STEPS/_FRAMES/_WORK/_RECURSE/_FLOOR (no per-prefix <PREFIX>_ERR_* spelling exists).
PCREC_ERR_FLOOR is -5 (it moved from -4 when PCREC_ERR_RECURSE joined the give-up codes).
PCREC_ERR_INTERNAL lives in the same shared ABI block but is below the floor and is NOT a give-up.
The caps-array unset sentinel is PCREC_UNSET (no <PREFIX>_UNSET).
The nine D46 stamp bit constants are spelled PCREC_VM_RUNG_*, PCREC_VM_STRAT_*, PCREC_VM_PRUNE_* (no per-prefix spelling).
The old per-prefix spellings of the moved macros are deleted, not aliased.
PCREC_ENGINE_DFA and PCREC_ENGINE_VM name the values of rx_info.engine.

What stays per-prefix is exactly the set whose value varies per artifact: <PREFIX>_NCAPS, the budget/capacity macros, the D46 stamp masks (<PREFIX>_VM_RUNGS/_STRATS/_PRUNES), <PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER and <PREFIX>_VM_PRUNE_CEILING.
Every artifact exports <prefix>_search_in, <prefix>_match_in and <prefix>_match_caps_in on both engines (inert on a DFA artifact).
Every artifact declares <prefix>_buffers and carries five sizing macros and four additional rx_info fields for the §10 caller-provided frame buffer, on both engines, inert on a DFA artifact.
Measured: <prefix>_search's stack frame is 131,216 B on a call-bearing artifact where <prefix>_search_in's is 144 B.
Measured: the give-up boundary of the §10 change is unmoved: a 684-byte subject matches and 686 does not (PCREC_ERR_FRAMES).
Measured: the MAP_NORESERVE worked example matches an 800 KB subject in 0.057 s touching 90 MB.
CHECK: rx_info.abi is 27 in the revision note's text (stale; the artifact's abi is 71 per the K80 guard example).
§4 points at docs/spec/limits.md for the numeric trigger defaults of the give-up codes.
Measured on --no-captures '(?:foo|bar)\z': RX_ENGINE "dfa", RX_DFA_SCAN "unanchored", RX_DFA_PREFILTER "byte-class-bounded" are present.
A consumer may #if on RX_ENGINE (the DFA stamp gap is discharged).
CHECK: every artifact of both engines has exactly one line in the shared prologue, #define <PREFIX>_TUNE "<token>", a closed five-token selection stamp of 23-28 bytes by token.
CHECK: at the default dial position balanced nothing else moves (every cell of that row in src/core/tune.c is the em-dash sentinel and its deny mask is empty).
CHECK: a non-default dial position may move far more than the stamp, but no struct offset moves, no rx_info member is added or changed, and no answer moves at any position.
CHECK: every scan-edge-bearing DFA machine (or VM-hybrid inlined prefilter) has a trailing ; on its scan_views and scan_edge labels (clang -Wc23-extensions fix); no answer moves.
Candidate match starts are character boundaries: every artifact carries #define PCREC_ERR_STARTPOS (-7) in the shared ABI block.
Under a multi-byte encoding the unanchored machine, ENG_ATTEMPT's start loop and the entries' boundary guard enforce that candidate match starts are character boundaries.
CHECK: the VM's ASCII-FOLD class test is described at §6.3's _VM_CLS_FOLDS entry and docs/spec/tuning.md §2.22.
CHECK: every VM artifact carries the <PREFIX>_VM_ENTRY_SHAPE and <PREFIX>_VM_PROGRAM_BYTES stamps.
CHECK: at VM entry-shape rungs shared/forward the three _in entries carry the body and the un-suffixed entries forward to them, with a static empty descriptor emitted.
CHECK: the scan-edge entry-seed dispatch is generalised to is_stop && !is_dead, and precondition (8) admits an edge only where the seed AND the prefilter reseeds.
CHECK: on a composed artifact groups[] gains the definitions' delivered rows under a leading SCOPE sort key, so nentries exceeds nnames; invisible on a non-composed compile.
CHECK: a flat alternation whose language is a finite literal set is emitted as a trie dispatch rather than vm_alt's serial resume chain, with a <PREFIX>_VM_ALT_ISLANDS count.
CHECK: always_inline is applied to a frameless VM artifact's entry-chain helpers, and the uniform-table fold carries a <PREFIX>_DFA_UNIFORM_FOLDS stamp.
CHECK: the start-pinned search is stamped by rx_info.search_form and <PREFIX>_DFA_START.
§8.2 states plainly, before its field table, which encodings are implemented (CHECK: the note says byte is the only one, stale since utf8 shipped).
§3.6 documents whole-subject / end-anchored matching via the (?:P)\z idiom.
There is no native end-anchored entry, so whole-subject matching is expressed as the (?:P)\z idiom.
$ is the wrong anchor for whole-subject matching: (?:foo)$ matches "foo\n" at [0,3) while (?:foo)\z on the same subject reports no match.
A naive _match_caps(...) == n test is sufficient but not necessary for whole-subject matching.
Measured: pattern a|ab on subject "ab" reports [0,1), while (?:a|ab)\z on the same subject reports [0,2) via the alternative the naive test never tries.
The (?:P)\z idiom is RULED permanent (D77, plan row [OS-4], 2026-08-25); it is not a stopgap awaiting a future generation axis.

Measured: whole-subject artifacts on --no-captures '(?:foo|bar)\z' and '(?:foo)\z' carry RX_DFA_SCAN "unanchored" and RX_DFA_PREFILTER "byte-class-bounded" / "memchr-bounded" respectively (the -bounded forms §6.3 documents for a \z view).
§3.1.1 states the utf8 advance as normative text: from pos + 1, past every byte in 0x80-0xBF.
The utf8 advance rule defines <prefix>_next_pos on ill-formed input, where "the next character boundary" had no single reading.
Every symbol a pattern compile can produce falls into one of three groups: per-artifact (prefix-scoped), pcrec's fixed library surface, and fixed-literal ABI types.
Boundary case: the two artifact-stamp macros PCREC_FEATURE_SET and PCREC_FEATURE_MODULES are PCREC_*-named yet per-artifact.
Per-artifact symbols are scoped by the caller's pcrec_options.prefix, default "rx".
<prefix>_search is a per-artifact symbol scoped by the prefix.
<prefix>_match is a per-artifact symbol scoped by the prefix.
<prefix>_match_caps is a per-artifact symbol scoped by the prefix.
<prefix>_info is a per-artifact symbol scoped by the prefix.
<prefix>_next_pos (§3.1.1) is a per-artifact symbol scoped by the prefix.
<prefix>_valid_upto (§3.1.2, [UTF-VALID]) is a per-artifact symbol scoped by the prefix.
The <PREFIX>_* macro family (RX_NCAPS and the D46 observability macros of §6.3) is scoped by the uppercased prefix.
A pattern compiled with -p foo gets foo_search and FOO_NCAPS (verified by reading the emitted header).
The CLI spells the prefix option -p and only -p; there is no --prefix long form and `pcrec --prefix foo ...` is an unknown-option error.
RX_UNSET and RX_ERR_* are not in the per-prefix family; they are the fixed unprefixed PCREC_* constants in the ABI block and no <PREFIX>_* spelling exists, no alias.
Group 2 is pcrec's own fixed library surface: the PCREC_* enum/bit constants and the pcrec_options, pcrec_output, pcrec_error and pcrec_err_input types declared in lib/pcrec.h.
The group-2 library surface is never scoped by a generated pattern's prefix.
The PCREC_* spelling is not by itself a promise that a name lives in lib/pcrec.h.
Every emitted artifact carries PCREC_FEATURE_SET (D37 artifact stamp, e.g. "std1").
Every emitted artifact carries PCREC_FEATURE_MODULES (D37 artifact stamp, e.g. "classes,modifiers").
PCREC_FEATURE_SET and PCREC_FEATURE_MODULES are PCREC_*-named, per-artifact, and declared nowhere in lib/pcrec.h.
PCREC_FEATURE_SET and PCREC_FEATURE_MODULES are the only exception to §8's naming rule; every other PCREC_* name follows it.
Group 3 is the fixed-literal ABI types, scoped by neither the caller's prefix nor pcrec's library surface.
The six group-3 types are rx_ctx, rx_matchfn, rx_callout_ref, rx_renderfn, rx_group_entry and struct rx_info, declared in that order.
The group-3 types are always spelled rx_* regardless of the prefix.
The fixed rx_* types let two differently-prefixed generated matchers compose in one translation unit (a compiled matcher links directly as another's callout, with no adapter).
The six group-3 types live inside their own #ifndef PCREC_RX_ABI_H guard, separate from the per-prefix PCREC_GEN_<PREFIX>_H guard wrapping the rest of the file.
Two artifacts compiled with different prefixes and #included into one TU declare the group-3 types identically and do not collide.
Confirmed: -p rx and -p foo builds of the same pattern emit byte-identical #ifndef PCREC_RX_ABI_H blocks.
K80 (abi 54): the value of the PCREC_RX_ABI_H guard macro is the abi number (e.g. #define PCREC_RX_ABI_H 71).
Every artifact's ABI block opens with #if defined(PCREC_RX_ABI_H) && (PCREC_RX_ABI_H + 0) != <abi> followed by an #error, then #ifndef PCREC_RX_ABI_H / #define PCREC_RX_ABI_H <abi>.
The #error text reads: "pcrec: this artifact (abi N) shares a translation unit with an artifact of a different abi; regenerate both with one pcrec".
Artifacts of one abi share the first ABI block in a TU.
An artifact of a different abi (whose types may differ) included into the same TU fails to compile via #error instead of silently using the first block's types.
The abi guard is one guard with a value, not a guard name per abi (two keyed guards would let both blocks through and fail on a struct redefinition).
The `+ 0` in the abi guard test makes it refuse a pre-54 artifact included first (whose guard is defined empty).
A pre-54 artifact included AFTER a 54-or-later one is not refused (its own #ifndef predates the rule).
The shared guarded ABI block carries every emitted macro whose value is a pcrec-contract fact, unprefixed.
The contract-fact macros are emitted unconditionally on every artifact, DFA-only included (reserved but unreachable).
The shared ABI block carries PCREC_ERR_STEPS, PCREC_ERR_FRAMES, PCREC_ERR_WORK, PCREC_ERR_RECURSE and PCREC_ERR_FLOOR (the give-up code space, §4).
PCREC_ERR_RECURSE joined the give-up codes and PCREC_ERR_FLOOR moved from -4 to -5 at [DD-14] wave A (D71 item 1).
The shared ABI block carries the below-the-floor PCREC_ERR_INTERNAL, which is NOT a give-up.
The shared ABI block carries PCREC_ERR_STARTPOS, PCREC_ERR_UNSET_VAR and PCREC_ERR_UTF, the caller-refusal siblings of PCREC_ERR_INTERNAL (§4).
The shared ABI block carries the caps-array unset sentinel PCREC_UNSET (§5).
The shared ABI block carries PCREC_ENGINE_DFA and PCREC_ENGINE_VM (§6).

The shared ABI block carries the nine D46 stamp bit constants PCREC_VM_RUNG_CURSOR/_FRAMES_BOUNDED/_FRAMES_UNBOUNDED/_REVDET/_COUNTER, PCREC_VM_STRAT_POSSESSIVE/_BACKTRACKING, PCREC_VM_PRUNE_CLAMPED/_UNCLAMPED (§6.3).
The old <PREFIX>_* spellings of the moved macros are deleted, not aliased.
What stays per-prefix is <PREFIX>_NCAPS plus the D46 stamp MASKS and the budget/capacity macros of §6.3, because their values vary per artifact.
A generated artifact is either self-contained (options.header_name == NULL, everything in the .c) or split into a paired .h/.c (options.header_name set).
Both the self-contained and the split form carry identical declarations.
The self-contained form omits the PCREC_GEN_<PREFIX>_H include guard entirely (there is no header to guard).
Measured with header_name == NULL: zero occurrences of the PCREC_GEN_<PREFIX>_H guard, against three in the split form's .h.
The D46 observability macros of §6.3 are emitted into the .c only, never into the .h.
rx_ctx.subject is `const unsigned char *`, the whole subject, not a slice.
rx_ctx.len is a size_t holding the subject length.
rx_ctx.pos is a size_t naming where to match, anchored.
rx_ctx.ncap is a size_t: the capture slots known so far (a watermark mid-match; ncaps on completion).
rx_ctx.caps is `const ptrdiff_t (*)[2]` holding [start,end) pairs; {-1,-1} means unset.
rx_ctx.user is a `void *` of per-binding user data.
An rx_matchfn returns the matched length >= 0 (anchored at ctx->pos), -1 on fail, or a typed give-up code in [PCREC_ERR_FLOOR, -2].
There is one typed give-up code per way the engine can give up (PCREC_ERR_STEPS/_FRAMES/_WORK/_RECURSE).
D49: give-up codes PROPAGATE through an rx_matchfn; they are not collapsed to -1, and a caller doing an exact `== -1` test sees them as distinct values.
Values strictly BELOW PCREC_ERR_FLOOR stay RESERVED for a future abort semantic.
PCREC_ERR_INTERNAL ([DD-14] wave A commit 2, D71 item 1) is the first producer of a below-the-floor value.
A generated call site that invokes an rx_matchfn traps on a below-the-floor return.
An rx_matchfn is self-contained: it must accept ctx->ncap == 0 and ctx->caps == NULL.
rx_matchfn is `typedef ptrdiff_t rx_matchfn(const rx_ctx *ctx)`.
PCREC_ERR_STEPS is (-2).
PCREC_ERR_FRAMES is (-3).
PCREC_ERR_WORK is (-4).
PCREC_ERR_RECURSE is (-5).
CHECK: PCREC_ERR_RECURSE is reserved with no producer yet (D71 item 1) per the emitted comment.
PCREC_ERR_FLOOR is (-5); give-ups occupy [FLOOR, -2]; values below are reserved (D49).
PCREC_ERR_INTERNAL is (-6); it is below PCREC_ERR_FLOOR and is NOT a give-up (D71 item 1).
PCREC_ERR_STARTPOS is (-7); it is below the floor and means a mid-character startpos was REFUSED ([K50]).
PCREC_ERR_UNSET_VAR is (-8); it is below the floor and means an UNSET or ill-formed variable value was REFUSED ([VAR]).
PCREC_ERR_UTF is (-9); it is below PCREC_ERR_FLOOR, NOT a give-up, and means an ill-formed subject was REFUSED (-futf-check; [UTF-VALID]).
PCREC_UNSET is ((ptrdiff_t)-1), the caps-array unset sentinel.
rx_callout_ref is a struct holding `rx_matchfn *fn` and `void *user`.
rx_renderfn is emitted ONLY when a substitution template names it.
An rx_renderfn renders one template segment from the same rx_ctx a callout receives.
An rx_renderfn writes at most outcap bytes to out and returns the number of bytes produced, or -1 to fail.
Called with out == NULL and outcap == 0, an rx_renderfn returns the length it WOULD produce and writes nothing.
rx_renderfn is `typedef ptrdiff_t rx_renderfn(const rx_ctx *ctx, unsigned char *out, size_t outcap)`.
rx_group_entry is a struct with fields `const char *name`, `int number`, `int slot`, `const char *ref`.
rx_group_entry.slot is the caps[] index this entry delivers, or -1 if this build delivers no slot for it.
rx_group_entry.ref is NULL/empty for the primary's own groups.

[DD-13b.W1.3] on a composed artifact (pcrec --source) an rx_group_entry row whose ref is non-NULL names the DEFINITION that declared the group; that row is a library's group seen by the caller (§6 composition).
struct rx_info's full field list is quoted in §6 (the §2 block elides its body).
PCREC_ENGINE_DFA is 1.
PCREC_ENGINE_VM is 2.
PCREC_VM_RUNG_CURSOR is 0x1u.
PCREC_VM_RUNG_FRAMES_BOUNDED is 0x2u.
PCREC_VM_RUNG_FRAMES_UNBOUNDED is 0x4u.
PCREC_VM_RUNG_REVDET is 0x8u.
PCREC_VM_RUNG_COUNTER is 0x10u.
PCREC_VM_STRAT_POSSESSIVE is 0x1u.
PCREC_VM_STRAT_BACKTRACKING is 0x2u.
PCREC_VM_PRUNE_CLAMPED is 0x1u.
PCREC_VM_PRUNE_UNCLAMPED is 0x2u.
`extern const struct rx_info <prefix>_info;` is per-prefix and lives OUTSIDE the PCREC_RX_ABI_H guard.
The §2 block is the emitted text verbatim except that the struct rx_info body is elided to §6 and the <prefix>_info extern is outside the guard.

rx_renderfn carries a sizing protocol (shipped ABI text): called with out == NULL and outcap == 0 it writes nothing and returns the length it would produce, so a caller can size a buffer before rendering.
The artifact documents rx_group_entry.ref only as "NULL/empty for the primary's own groups"; the composed-artifact producer is specified in §6.
Every macro in the §2 ABI block is UNPREFIXED and byte-identical across every --prefix.
The rx_matchfn comment carries no <PREFIX> placeholder, because the macros it names no longer vary per artifact.
The nine D46 stamp bit constants and the two engine constants (PCREC_ENGINE_DFA/_VM) are emitted unconditionally, even on a DFA-only artifact that never produces a VM stamp value or a give-up code.
<PREFIX> still appears elsewhere in the artifact: struct rx_info's ncaps field comment reads "this artifact's own <PREFIX>_NCAPS".
<PREFIX>_NCAPS is a per-artifact VALUE and stays per-prefix on purpose.
rx_info is a struct TAG, not a typedef; every reference spells `struct rx_info`.
No bare `rx_info` typedef exists anywhere in an emitted header (it emits `struct rx_info { ... };` and `extern const struct rx_info <prefix>_info;`).

Under the default prefix "rx" the per-artifact instance <prefix>_info is the identifier rx_info, byte-identical to the type's name, so a typedef of that name cannot coexist with it; struct tags live in a separate C namespace so `struct rx_info` and the instance rx_info coexist.
An embedder writing code against a generated header declares `const struct rx_info *`, never a bare `rx_info`.
The struct-tag spelling of rx_info is RULED, not provisional (D57, 2026-08-18); the design sketch's typedef form is dead.
A consumer wanting a typedef'd name ships `typedef struct rx_info rx_info_t;` in its own header, which touches nothing pcrec emits.
Every generated artifact exports, unconditionally, five <prefix>-scoped entry symbols: the four specified below plus the encoding residual <prefix>_next_pos.
<prefix>_next_pos (§3.1.1, since [M5-SEAM]) is the one place an artifact's byte-vs-character distinction lives.
Every artifact also exports <prefix>_search_in, <prefix>_match_in and <prefix>_match_caps_in (D71 item 2), each its un-suffixed sibling plus one argument naming where the working storage lives.
An artifact exports eight entry symbols in total.
§10 is the contract of the three _in entries.
The three un-suffixed entries are unchanged in signature, return space and behaviour for a caller that never calls an _in entry (§10 promise).
[OPT-1]: the three un-suffixed entries have a cost model.
On an artifact whose stamped default storage does not fit inside one 4 KB page, each un-suffixed entry runs the match on a page-sized buffer.
Such an entry escalates to the stamped default storage only on a PCREC_ERR_FRAMES give-up.
Escalation calls a non-inlined internal function that owns the full storage and re-runs the match from scratch.
The tiering leaves unchanged the signatures, return spaces, anchoring, caps disciplines, every answer and every capture span of the un-suffixed entries (§10.9 proves it).
What tiering changes is only the price of a call.
Measured on the RFC 5322 email specimen (--engine=vm, 16-byte matching subject, N=100k): 213-268 ns/call before tiering to 45.6-48.8 after, against 44.2-47.2 for <prefix>_search_in.
Measured: the RFC 5322 specimen's entry frame (gcc -fstack-usage) shrinks from 98,512 B to 3,168 B under tiering.
Measured: the ^(a(?1)?b)$ recursion specimen's frame shrinks from 131,216 B to 3,184 B (the numbers used by §5.3 and limits.md §5).
Timing and frame numbers of different specimens must not be paired.
The tiered-entry bet loses on some patterns.
The wasted fast attempt is bounded by the STEP and WORK budgets, not by the frame count.
Sixty frames of depth can absorb an unbounded amount of backtracking, so the small fast tier does not bound the work it does before giving up.
There is a discontinuity at the tier boundary, not a ramp.
Measured on ((a)|(aa))+b (tiered vs -fno-tiered-entry, N=20k, median of 5): 18.5 vs 207.1 ns at n=1 (11x faster tiered).
Measured on ((a)|(aa))+b: 186.4 vs 365.3 ns at n=23 (tiered vs single-tier).
Measured on ((a)|(aa))+b: 568.9 vs 372.9 ns at n=24, a 3.05x jump across one byte and 1.53x slower than the single-tier entry.
Measured on ((a)|(aa))+b: above the boundary the tiered entry stays 1.24-1.53x slower than single-tier.
Measured: the ((a)|(aa))+b boundary is a 25-byte subject (24 a's and a b).
Depth is a property of the backtracking, not of the input length; "deep" can mean a very short subject.
An escalating call can do up to twice the STEP budget of real work, because §10.9 resets both budgets for the deep attempt and the fast attempt's spend is additional.
§4 states the consequence of the double budget spend for the give-up codes.
A caller that needs depth on the fast path uses an _in entry, supplying its own storage (§10), and never meets the tier.
A caller on a stack too small for the deep tier (§5.3, K33) should supply its own storage through the _in entries.
-fno-tiered-entry (docs/spec/tuning.md §2.12) restores the single-tier entry shape without changing call sites.
-fno-tiered-entry is the right choice for a workload measured to sit above the tier boundary.
